[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.4.1 - repair[/b][/size]

If you installed 0.4.0 and went to Quinn the herbalist for his wasp stingers or the lava
troll hide, you could not do it. He asks, you agree, and nothing happens -- the turn-in never
appears. Two of that release's three errands were uncompletable, and I did not know until
somebody played them.

[b]Fixt[/b] is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt: it
fixes what is broken, restores what was cut, and adds new content only where the game plainly
ran out. This release is entirely the first of those, and it repairs the mod's own past
releases rather than the game's.

[size=125][b]What is fixed[/b][/size]

[b]Quinn's second and third errands now start.[/b] The replies offering them carried the
check deciding whether to show the option, and nothing to actually begin the quest. The first
errand was wired correctly, which is why the wolf pelts worked and the rest silently did not.

[b]47 broken replies across six conversations, going back to 0.2.0.[/b] A reply in a
Lionheart conversation file must be preceded by a blank line -- the shipped game does this
10,915 times without exception, and the parser depends on it. Without the separator the reply
is swallowed into the one before it and whatever it was meant to do never runs. It fails
silently. The conversation looks fine and a quest just does not move.

Every tool I had written for editing conversations was quietly dropping that line.

[b]The Sacred Scimitar hand-in.[/b] In 0.3.0 this was reported unreachable twice, and twice I
moved it somewhere more visible. The move was right both times -- the node it landed in was
malformed. That is the real fix, and it is in this release.

[b]Esteban's contract updates its journal.[/b] Kill him for the goblins and the log used to
still say "kill him". The quest always completed; only the entry was wrong.

[size=125][b]The part I would rather write about[/b][/size]

None of these were found by the checks. The mod has an automated validator that runs before
every build, and it passed all three releases with these defects in them, because it checked
that files parsed and that references resolved -- not that a reply was shaped the way the
engine requires, or that a quest this mod defines is ever actually started.

Both checks exist now, and both were verified by deliberately breaking something first. The
second one found the Esteban bug on its first run.

The wider lesson, for anyone modding this game: [b]restoring content runs code that has never
executed.[/b] Vanilla's own quests are full of paths that were written, wired, and never
walked, and the moment you make one reachable you are the first person to test it. A
validator that only proves the files are well-formed will not tell you that.

[size=125][b]Installing[/b][/size]

Download, unzip, run [i]Mod Manager.bat[/i]. It finds a GOG, Steam or retail install by
itself and [i]Uninstall[/i] puts everything back.

Install over 0.4.0 as normal. [b]These fixes apply to an existing save[/b] -- conversations
are read fresh each time you speak to someone, unlike map contents, which a save records the
first time it loads a level. If you were stuck on Quinn's stingers or the hide, just ask him
again.

Sewers faction work -- making peace with the lava trolls, ransoming the lost boy instead of
fighting for him, and three errands for the troll chief -- is written and is the next
release. It is not in this one.
